title: OAuth Handoff Token Replay - Server-Side Single-Use Enforcement Not Verifiable
boundary: Mobile App → Web Backend (/api/mobile/exchange)
lower_trust_principal: Attacker with access to deep link token (clipboard, notification preview, browser history, logs)
affected_resource: User's Google OAuth session / Supabase RLS JWT / Cloud account access
attack_scenario: Attacker captures the 32-char hex handoff nonce from clipboard, notification preview, or browser history and replays it to /api/mobile/exchange to obtain a valid Supabase RLS JWT, granting full cloud account access.
evidence: src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:270-293 — USED_HANDOFF_TOKENS_KEY journal, markHandoffTokenUsed/isHandoffTokenUsed with 24h TTL and 50-entry cap; comment 'Best-effort; server enforces single-use'
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:997-1027 — completeGoogleHandoff checks isHandoffTokenUsed BEFORE googleExchange, marks AFTER success (non-atomic check-then-act)
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:1040-1057 — Linking listener cold-start path extracts token from sahakarisip://auth/callback?token= and calls googleHandoffRef.current directly
app/(auth)/auth/callback.tsx:31-38 — Warm handoff path: resolveGoogleHandoff resolves waiters, callback screen reflects resulting auth state
src/lib/auth/mobileApi.ts:87-94 — googleStart generates 32-char hex nonce client-side via expo-crypto getRandomBytes(16)
src/lib/auth/mobileApi.ts:97-100 — googleExchange POSTs nonce to /api/mobile/exchange; no client-side proof of server-side single-use
root_cause: Critical single-use enforcement relies on server-side logic in separate repository (sahakari-sip web backend) that cannot be audited from mobile codebase. Client-side journal is best-effort only.
recommended_remediation: Add server-side audit to verify /api/mobile/exchange atomically consumes and invalidates the handoff token. Implement nonce binding to device fingerprint or session. Consider PKCE for mobile OAuth flows.
needs_validation: Verify web backend /api/mobile/exchange implements atomic single-use consumption
Confirm token invalidation on first use (prevents replay)
Check if web backend binds nonce to IP/user-agent/device
Verify web backend rate-limits exchange endpoint

title: Native Google Sign-In - Server-Side ID Token Validation Not Verifiable
boundary: Mobile App → Web Backend (/api/mobile/google-native)
lower_trust_principal: Mobile App (untrusted client running on user device)
affected_resource: Web Backend authentication service / user accounts in next_auth.users
attack_scenario: If the web backend /api/mobile/google-native fails to verify the ID token's aud/iss/exp/signature, an attacker with a valid Google ID token for a different audience (or a forged token) could authenticate as any user.
evidence: src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:1097 — hardcoded webClientId fallback used in GoogleSignin.configure()
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:1102 — idToken extracted from userInfo.data?.idToken
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:1103-1108 — only null/undefined check, no JWT validation
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:1113 — googleNativeSignIn(idToken) called with raw token
src/lib/auth/mobileApi.ts:109-114 — googleNativeSignIn() POSTs {idToken} to /google-native
root_cause: Mobile client sends raw Google ID token without client-side validation of audience, issuer, expiry, or signature. Server-side validation at web backend cannot be verified from mobile repository.
recommended_remediation: Add server-side audit to verify /api/mobile/google-native validates: aud=webClientId, iss=accounts.google.com, exp > now, valid Google signature. Consider client-side pre-validation as defense-in-depth.
needs_validation: Verify web backend /api/mobile/google-native validates ID token aud/iss/exp/signature
Confirm webClientId matches Google Cloud Console Android client config
Check if web backend uses Google's tokeninfo endpoint or local JWKS verification

title: Android ADB Backup Exfiltrates Supabase JWT and Device-Local Credentials via SharedPreferences
boundary: Device (USB/ADB) → App Private Storage
lower_trust_principal: Physical device holder with ADB/USB access
affected_resource: Supabase RLS JWT (accessToken), device-local password hashes/vault metadata, session identity, OAuth replay tokens
attack_scenario: Attacker with physical device access runs 'adb backup -all com.samimrrza.sahakarisip' and extracts the backup. Using abe.jar, they unpack the backup and read all SharedPreferences including sahakarisip.v1.mobile_session (Supabase RLS JWT), sahakarisip.v1.session (user identity), sahakarisip.v1.profiles (password hashes/salts/vault), and sahakarisip.v1.used_handoff_tokens.
evidence: android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:20 — android:allowBackup="false" with comment warning expo prebuild reverts it
android/app/src/main/res/xml/secure_store_backup_rules.xml:5-6 — <include domain="sharedpref" path="."/> <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="SecureStore"/>
android/app/src/main/res/xml/secure_store_data_extraction_rules.xml:6-7,10-11 — Same include-all sharedprefs pattern for cloud-backup and device-transfer
src/lib/auth/mobileSession.ts:35,55-81 — SESSION_KEY="sahakarisip.v1.mobile_session" stores MobileSession with accessToken (Supabase RLS JWT) and expiresAt in AsyncStorage
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:190-192,420-429 — SESSION_KEY="sahakarisip.v1.session" stores AppUser (id, email, name, avatarUrl, mode) and SESSION_STARTED_KEY timestamp in AsyncStorage
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:233-244 — PROFILES_KEY="sahakarisip.v1.profiles" stores LocalProfile[] with salt, hash, iterations, vault (wrapped DEKs) in AsyncStorage
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:272-292 — USED_HANDOFF_TOKENS_KEY="sahakarisip.v1.used_handoff_tokens" stores replay-protection tokens in AsyncStorage
src/lib/auth/local-vault.ts:32,178-188 — SECURESTORE_PREFIX="sahakarisip.v1.dek." stores DEKs in SecureStore (correctly excluded)
root_cause: Backup rules explicitly include all SharedPreferences (domain=sharedpref path=.) while only excluding SecureStore. The only protection is android:allowBackup=false which expo prebuild reverts to true.
recommended_remediation: Change backup rules to exclude all sahakarisip.* SharedPreferences keys. Add explicit <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="sahakarisip"/> rules. Add CI check to prevent allowBackup=true in Manifest. Store all sensitive data in SecureStore/Keystore, not AsyncStorage.

title: Local Vault - PBKDF2 Iterations (100k) Below 2026 Security Baseline
boundary: Device User → Local Encrypted Vault
lower_trust_principal: Attacker with vault metadata (salt, wrapped DEK) and offline compute
affected_resource: User's password-wrapped DEK (and all local vault data)
attack_scenario: Attacker extracts the vault metadata (wrap_salt, wrapped_dek_password) from AsyncStorage and performs offline brute-force attack on the password. At 100k iterations, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 is ~6x below 2024-2026 baseline (NIST SP 800-63B: 600k; OWASP: 600k minimum), reducing effective password entropy by ~2.5 bits.
evidence: src/lib/auth/local-vault.ts:29 — const WRAP_ITERATIONS = 100_000
src/lib/auth/local-vault.ts:88-90 — passwordWrapKeyBytes uses pbkdf2Bytes with WRAP_ITERATIONS
src/lib/auth/nativeCrypto.ts:82-93 — pbkdf2Bytes calls quickCrypto().pbkdf2Sync (native) / WebCrypto (web) with iterations parameter
root_cause: PBKDF2 iteration count of 100,000 was adequate ~2018 but is significantly below current 2026 baselines (600k+). The native crypto shim (react-native-quick-crypto) supports higher iterations.
recommended_remediation: Increase WRAP_ITERATIONS to 600,000 (OWASP 2026 minimum) or 1,000,000 (NIST SP 800-63B). Test performance impact on target devices. Add versioning to vault format to allow iterative upgrades for existing users.

title: Biometric Unlock Resets Client TTL Without Server-Side Token Validation
boundary: OS Biometric Prompt → SecureStore Session Entry → Supabase RLS JWT
lower_trust_principal: Local biometric sensor / OS authentication subsystem
affected_resource: MobileSession (Supabase RLS JWT + user identity) stored in SecureStore
attack_scenario: User's JWT is revoked server-side (password change, admin revoke, security event). User authenticates via biometric; app restores stale JWT from SecureStore and resets client-side 4-hour TTL without any server-side token validation. The user remains authenticated until a Supabase request fails.
evidence: src/lib/auth/biometric.ts:106 disableDeviceFallback: true correctly prevents PIN/pattern fallback
src/lib/auth/biometric.ts:53-56 SecureStore.setItemAsync stores BiometricEntry with mobileSession (JWT) or localProfileId — Keystore/Enclave backed
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:650-654 unlockWithBiometric checks entry.mobileSession.expiresAt <= now (JWT expiry) before restore
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:658-660 TTL reset: new SESSION_STARTED_KEY written after biometric unlock, granting fresh 4-hour window
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:1359 signOut calls clearBiometricEntry() — biometric entry does NOT survive explicit signOut
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:1380-1415 expireSession stashes current mobileSession to biometric entry on TTL expiry, then sets status=locked for biometric re-auth
root_cause: Stateless JWT design means server-side revocation cannot be instantly enforced on biometric unlock. The app trusts the stored JWT until a Supabase request fails.
recommended_remediation: On biometric unlock, make a lightweight Supabase API call (e.g., getUser()) to validate the JWT is still active before resetting TTL. Implement short JWT lifetime (15-30 min) with refresh token rotation for better revocation granularity.
needs_validation: Confirm JWT lifetime (expiresAt) aligns with acceptable staleness window
Verify Supabase RLS JWT revocation propagation latency
Assess whether 4-hour client TTL + biometric TTL reset extends session beyond intended maximum

title: Session TTL Only Enforced on Foreground Transition - Bypass by Keeping App Active
boundary: App Runtime → Session State (absolute 4-hour TTL boundary)
lower_trust_principal: Attacker with physical access to unlocked device (or malware with foreground execution)
affected_resource: User session (cloud Supabase RLS JWT or local vault DEK)
attack_scenario: Attacker with physical access to unlocked device keeps the app in foreground continuously. The absolute 4-hour TTL is only checked on AppState background→active transition. The session never expires, effectively bypassing the banking-style absolute expiry guarantee.
evidence: src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:257-261 (SESSION_TTL_MS = 4*60*60*1000 constant)
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:386-418 (AppState listener — TTL check ONLY at lines 391-400 when nextState==='active' AND prev!=='active')
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:1380-1418 (expireSession — biometric stash vs full logout)
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:698-700 (bootstrap also checks TTL on cold start)
root_cause: TTL enforcement is event-driven (AppState change) rather than time-driven (periodic timer). Biometric users get effective session extension via stashed re-auth.
recommended_remediation: Add a periodic timer (e.g., setInterval every 5 min) that checks TTL regardless of AppState. On TTL expiry, call expireSession immediately even in foreground. This enforces the absolute 4-hour boundary as documented.

title: Recovery Key Displayed/Entered in Plaintext Without Screen Capture Protection
boundary: Device User → Recovery Key Input → Vault DEK
lower_trust_principal: Device User (shoulder-surfer, screenshot/recording malware, clipboard-accessing apps)
affected_resource: Device-local account vault DEK (full decryption of all local portfolio data)
attack_scenario: The 128-bit recovery key is displayed in plaintext at signup (large font, bold) and entered in plaintext during password reset (no secureTextEntry). No screen capture prevention is active despite expo-screen-capture being installed. Clipboard copy exposes key to system clipboard. Attacker with visual access or clipboard access captures the recovery key and fully decrypts the local vault.
evidence: src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:936-954 — signUp creates vault and returns recoveryKey in AuthResult
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:1257-1312 — resetLocalPassword accepts recoveryKey in plaintext, calls unwrapWithRecoveryKey
src/components/auth/RecoveryKeyOnce.tsx:29 — Clipboard.setStringAsync(recoveryKey) copies key to system clipboard
src/components/auth/RecoveryKeyOnce.tsx:79 — Recovery key rendered in plaintext: {recoveryKey} with fontSize: lg, fontWeight: 800
app/(auth)/signup.tsx:117-122,160-177 — On device-mode signup, recoveryKey stored in state and RecoveryKeyOnce rendered
app/(auth)/login.tsx:227-234 — Forgot password recovery key Input lacks secureTextEntry, autoCapitalize=characters
app/(auth)/login.tsx:201-268 — Forgot password flow for local mode displays recovery key input in plaintext
package.json — expo-screen-capture:~57.0.3 installed but NOT imported/used anywhere in src/
src/lib/auth/local-vault.ts:62-64,67-69,140-151 — Recovery key normalized, SHA-256 hashed for verification, used directly as AES-256-GCM key wrapper
root_cause: Recovery key displayed and entered in plaintext without secureTextEntry or screen capture protection. expo-screen-capture is installed but preventScreenCaptureAsync() is never called.
recommended_remediation: Add secureTextEntry to recovery key input fields. Call ScreenCapture.preventScreenCaptureAsync() on screens displaying/entering recovery key. Remove clipboard copy or make it optional with clear warning. Mask recovery key display (show only first/last 4 chars).

title: CSV Import - Naive Parser (split) Without RFC 4180 Support, No File Size Limit
boundary: User Input (CSV file) → Parsed Data → Validated Entries → Database
lower_trust_principal: Untrusted user-supplied CSV file via expo-document-picker
affected_resource: SahakariSIP entries table (Supabase/AsyncStorage), fund NAV history, dashboard computations
attack_scenario: Attacker crafts malicious CSV with quoted commas, embedded newlines, or scientific notation that bypasses the naive split(',') parser, causing field confusion, data corruption, or DoS via unbounded file read into memory.
evidence: src/components/entries/CsvImportModal.tsx:70-148 — parseCsv() uses split(',') without RFC 4180 support (no quoted field handling, no escaped quotes, no embedded newlines)
src/components/entries/CsvImportModal.tsx:162 — FileSystem.readAsStringAsync(asset.uri) reads entire file with no size limit
src/components/entries/CsvImportModal.tsx:68 — MAX_IMPORT_ROWS=2000 only limits rows after parsing, not file size
src/lib/schemas/entry.ts:54-57 — date validation uses new Date(val) which accepts ambiguous formats
src/lib/schemas/entry.ts:58-60 — z.coerce.number() accepts scientific notation (e.g., '1e1000' → Infinity, caught by .finite(); but '1e10' → 10000000000 passes)
src/lib/data/cloud.ts:630-722 — importEntriesFromCsv validates via csvRowSchema.safeParse but trusts parsed output
src/lib/data/local.ts:552-641 — importEntriesFromCsv same validation path as cloud
root_cause: Custom CSV parser uses naive split(',') without RFC 4180 compliance. No file size limit before parsing. Zod schema allows scientific notation in numeric fields.
recommended_remediation: Replace custom parser with RFC 4180 compliant library (e.g., PapaParse). Add file size limit (e.g., 1MB) before reading. Restrict numeric fields to fixed-point decimal regex. Add server-side row count and payload size limits.

affected_resource: User's Expo push token + userId (PII + notification capability)
attack_scenario: Attacker compromises the Vercel deployment or hijacks the domain, harvests all users' push tokens, and sends arbitrary notifications. Push token is a bearer credential - anyone with it can send pushes to that device.

title: Local Vault - encryptJson Returns Plaintext When Vault Is Locked
boundary: App Runtime → Encrypted AsyncStorage
lower_trust_principal: Locked/Unauthenticated App Runtime (vault locked, no active DEK)
affected_resource: All local encrypted data store payloads (funds, entries, nav_history, prefs, notifications, profile) written via writeJson/encryptJson
attack_scenario: When the vault is locked (activeDek === null), encryptJson() returns the plaintext JSON string instead of encrypting it. Any write operation (createFundConfig, createEntry, updateFundConfig, saveNotificationPreferences, updateProfileImage, etc.) persists unencrypted sensitive financial data to AsyncStorage. Subsequent unlock does not re-encrypt existing plaintext records.
evidence: src/lib/auth/local-vault.ts:201-208 — encryptJson() returns raw json when !activeDek
src/lib/data/local.ts:89-92 — writeJson() calls encryptJson() for all data writes
src/lib/data/local.ts:107-129 — All CRUD operations (funds, entries, nav, prefs, notifications, profile) route through writeJson()
root_cause: encryptJson() has a fallback to return plaintext when no active DEK, intended for legacy migration but creates a security hole when vault is locked during normal operation.
recommended_remediation: Change encryptJson() to throw an error when vault is locked instead of returning plaintext. Add vault state check before any write operation. Ensure vault is unlocked before LocalStore methods execute (they're only called after authentication).
needs_validation: Confirm vault can be locked during normal app operation (e.g., after logout, background timeout, or explicit lockVault())
Verify no auto-unlock logic runs before writes in LocalStore methods
Test: lock vault → call createFundConfig → inspect AsyncStorage for plaintext
Check if NAV_AUTO_KEY/NAV_LAST_SYNC_KEY plaintext storage is acceptable (low-sensitivity metadata)

title: NPM Transitive Dependencies - 27 Vulnerabilities (1 Critical, 17 High, 9 Moderate)
boundary: Dependency Supply Chain → Application Runtime
lower_trust_principal: Transitive NPM dependencies (shell-quote@1.10.0, node-forge@1.4.0, braces@3.0.3, micromatch@4.0.8, react-native-reanimated@4.5.1, react-native-worklets@0.10.1, metro@0.84.6, @expo/* packages)

title: Web Backend Handoff Token Single-Use Enforcement Not Verifiable
boundary: Mobile App → Web Backend (/api/mobile/exchange)
lower_trust_principal: Mobile Client (untrusted, user-controlled device)
affected_resource: Web Backend OAuth handoff token consumption endpoint
attack_scenario: If the web backend does not atomically consume and invalidate the handoff token, an attacker who intercepts the sahakarisip://auth/callback?token=... redirect could replay it to obtain a valid Supabase RLS JWT.
evidence: src/lib/auth/mobileApi.ts:97-100 - googleExchange() POSTs nonce to /api/mobile/exchange
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:270-293 - Client-side handoff token journal (USED_HANDOFF_TOKENS_KEY) with TTL and cap
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:291 - Comment: 'Best-effort; server enforces single-use.'
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:266-267 - Comment: 'completeGoogleHandoff dedupes the exchange (the token is single-use server-side too)'
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:998-1002 - completeGoogleHandoff() checks isHandoffTokenUsed() before exchange
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:1004-1005 - Calls googleExchange(token) then markHandoffTokenUsed(token)
root_cause: Server-side single-use enforcement is a critical OAuth/OIDC security control that cannot be verified from the mobile repository.
recommended_remediation: Add server-side audit of /api/mobile/exchange in sahakari-sip web backend repo. Verify atomic token consumption and invalidation.
needs_validation: Verify web backend /api/mobile/exchange implements atomic single-use consumption
Confirm token invalidation on first use
Check if web backend logs replay attempts

title: Google ID Token Server-Side Validation Not Verifiable

lower_trust_principal: Mobile App (unverified client)
affected_resource: Web Backend Google ID token validation endpoint
attack_scenario: Mobile client sends raw Google ID token to /api/mobile/google-native without client-side validation. Server-side validation (audience, issuer, expiry, signature) cannot be verified from mobile repository.

recommended_remediation: Add server-side audit of /api/mobile/google-native in sahakari-sip web backend repo. Verify audience=webClientId, issuer=accounts.google.com, expiry, signature validation.
needs_validation: Verify web backend /api/mobile/google-native validates ID token aud/iss/exp/signature
Confirm webClientId matches Google Cloud Console Android client config

title: Screen Capture Prevention - Properly Implemented Globally

lower_trust_principal: Malicious app / screen recorder / screenshot tool / shoulder surfer
affected_resource: All app screens including auth (login, signup, forgot-password, lock), recovery key display (RecoveryKeyOnce), and authenticated app screens

title: Email Enumeration via Differentiated Auth Error Messages
boundary: Mobile App → Web Backend credential verification
lower_trust_principal: Unauthenticated mobile app user (attacker-controlled input, untrusted network)
affected_resource: User account existence and authentication state
attack_scenario: Attacker uses signin/signup error messages to enumerate valid email addresses. Signin differentiates 'email not confirmed' vs 'invalid credentials'. Signup passes through server error 'email already exists'. No client-side rate limiting on auth endpoints.
evidence: src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:835-848 — signIn differentiates 'email not confirmed' vs 'invalid credentials' error messages
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:918-922 — signup passes through server error messages directly (e.g., 'email already exists')
src/lib/auth/mobileApi.ts:118-123 — passwordLogin sends email+password in plaintext JSON body over HTTPS
src/lib/auth/mobileApi.ts:125-129 — signup sends email+password+confirmPassword to /api/mobile/signup over HTTPS
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:903-908 — Only client-side validation is password length >= 8 and password match; no complexity requirements
src/lib/auth/mobileApi.ts:33-63 — request() function has no retry/backoff, no rate-limit handling, no certificate pinning
src/lib/auth/mobileApi.ts:13-19 — WEB_URL defaults to https://sahakari-sip.vercel.app; isWebConfigured only checks https:// prefix
root_cause: Differentiated error messages leak account existence. No client-side rate limiting. Weak password policy (8 chars only).
recommended_remediation: Use generic error messages ('invalid credentials' for both wrong password and unconfirmed email). Implement client-side rate limiting with exponential backoff. Add password complexity requirements. Consider certificate pinning for auth endpoints.
needs_validation: Confirm server-side rate limiting exists on /api/mobile/password-login and /api/mobile/signup
Verify server returns generic error messages for email enumeration
Confirm bcrypt verification is server-side only
Verify OTP email confirmation is enforced before first signin

title: Password Reset Token Stored in Long-Lived React Ref Without Client-Side Lifecycle Management
boundary: Mobile App → Web Backend (OTP verification & password reset)
lower_trust_principal: Mobile App (untrusted client environment)
affected_resource: User account takeover via password reset flow
attack_scenario: The resetToken returned by verifyResetOtp is stored in a long-lived React ref (resetTokenRef.current) with no client-side invalidation on background, failed attempts, time expiry, or sign-out. An attacker with access to the running app memory can extract the valid resetToken and complete password reset without the OTP.
evidence: src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:350 - resetTokenRef = useRef({ token: null, email: null }) holds resetToken in memory for component lifetime
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:1519-1522 - verifyPasswordResetOtp stores result.resetToken and result.email in resetTokenRef.current
src/lib/auth/AuthContext.tsx:1551-1559 - completePasswordReset reads token from resetTokenRef.current, uses storedEmail for binding, clears ref only on success
src/lib/auth/mobileApi.ts:149-156 - verifyResetOtp returns { resetToken, email } from server; throws if no resetToken
src/lib/auth/mobileApi.ts:158-168 - completeReset requires email, resetToken, newPassword, confirmPassword
root_cause: Reset token stored in long-lived React ref with no client-side TTL, invalidation on background/signout, or failed attempt tracking.
recommended_remediation: Add client-side TTL for resetToken (e.g., 10 min). Invalidate on AppState background, signOut, or failed completeReset attempt. Store resetToken in SecureStore with expiry instead of React ref. Server-side must enforce single-use and short TTL.
needs_validation: Server-side resetToken TTL and single-use enforcement
Server-side OTP rate limiting (6-digit)
Server-side brute-force protection on verifyResetOtp endpoint
Whether resetToken is cryptographically bound to email/server-session
